original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Accelerate the complete four-command PR6208 Clifford replay by an exact signed packed Gaussian matrix kernel.
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card is specialized to a new arithmetic implementation; no predecessor theorem is audited or extended.
bottleneck_link: Verifier engineering side result: retain complete finite matrix coverage while reducing repeated exact replay cost. It changes no paid supplier invoice or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop at the first complete-suite gain outside observed ranges, or hand off an inconclusive result. No second arithmetic optimization.
evidence: 85 literal products / 21760 entries; 16275 signed vector pairs; 71 matrix cases; 11 invalid inputs; five source mutations; five alternating complete bundles per side, 40 commands, zero errors and output mismatches.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does this bounded packed kernel improve another actual Gaussian-rational checker with larger numerator components?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The observed gain is small in absolute time and is specific to one complete suite.
open_questions.first_step: Profile one different complete checker and measure integer packing width before adapting this source-bound runner.
open_questions.blocked_by: No performance or coverage evidence is supplied for another consumer.

overlap.scope: Live open PR list, own latest 200 PRs, last 40 handoffs, active discussions, replay-runtime overlap helper, main README and merged PR searches for order-seventeen, Gaussian multiplication and sparse multiplication.
overlap.limitations: No exhaustive historical novelty claim; only the bounded arithmetic implementation and measured consumer improvement are claimed.

claim_type: scoped implementation proof with measured local performance improvement
